punchline: Survivors of the same wreck came home with two stories that blamed each other.
thirty_sec: In 1741 HMS Wager was wrecked off southern Chile. One group of survivors, led by gunner John Bulkeley, sailed to Brazil. Others, including Captain Cheap and John Byron, returned later by a different route. Back in England, each group's account blamed the other, and the Admiralty held a court martial that ended without punishing the mutiny. David Grann tells this in The Wager.
